To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TFP differences among countries are driven by differences in the labor market institutions and that the effect of hiring subsidy policy depends on the labor market institutions.

(1) TFP is lower in continental European countries because of higher unemployment rates, and that (2) TFP increases when hiring subsidies are implemented, and this effect is larger in countries with lower TFP.
the TFP of continental European countries is lower than the TFP of Nordic countries because of higher skill losses during unemployment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of unemployment and job search on aggregate productivity.
the role of unemployment in the determination of aggregate productivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hiring subsidies are a good policy to improve TFP and the functioning of the labor market, but that the effect of the policy depends on the country’s labor market characteristics.
TFP differences among developed countries are mainly due to labor market institutions, but that hiring subsidies are a second best instrument to improve TFP.
the effect of hiring incentives on TFP is not clear cut and that the effect on the labor market is not necessarily negative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TFP differences across countries are mainly explained by differences in the labor market institutions, and that hiring subsidies are a good policy option for increasing TFP and reducing unemployment.
the Nordic countries are the best candidates to receive hiring subsidies.
the Nordic model is the best one in the sample of countries analyzed here.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the labor market policy should be evaluated not only in terms of its impact on unemployment but also in terms of its effect on TFP.
the design of labor market policy needs to be carefully tailored to the institutional environment in which it is implemented.
the labor market is a key determinant of the level of TFP in the economy.
